stem: Where is a vessel's center of gravity (G)?

options.text: The point through which the total weight can be considered to act
The geometric center of the propeller
The center of the rudder stock

explanation: The center of gravity is the point through which the resultant force of the vessel's weight acts.

source.label: USCG NMC sample examination topics - Q348

stem: Where does the resultant buoyant force act on a floating vessel?

options.text: At the center of gravity by definition
At the center of lateral resistance only

explanation: The center of buoyancy is the center of the displaced underwater volume and the point through which the resultant upward buoyant force acts.

source.label: USCG NMC sample examination topics - Q348

stem: What generally happens when heavy cargo is moved higher in a vessel?

options.text: The center of gravity automatically lowers
The metacenter becomes fixed at the deck

explanation: Moving weight higher raises the overall center of gravity and ordinarily reduces initial stability if other factors remain constant.

source.label: USCG NMC sample examination topics - Q348

stem: How does a partially filled wide tank affect a vessel's initial stability?

options.text: It creates a free-surface effect that tends to reduce initial stability
It has no effect unless salt water is used

explanation: The liquid surface can shift as the vessel heels, producing a virtual rise in center of gravity and reduced stability.

source.label: USCG NMC sample examination topics - Q348

stem: Which factor particularly increases the free-surface effect of liquid in a tank?

options.text: A large transverse breadth of free liquid surface
A lower liquid density in every case regardless of geometry

explanation: Free-surface moment increases strongly with the breadth of an unconfined liquid surface; full or empty tanks have no comparable free surface.

source.label: USCG NMC sample examination topics - Q348

stem: If a vessel's transverse metacentric height GM is positive for small angles, what does that generally indicate?
explanation: Positive GM indicates a tendency to develop a restoring moment for small heel angles, subject to the broader stability curve.

source.label: USCG NMC sample examination topics - Q348

stem: If the metacenter M and center of gravity G are at the same height for small angles, what is GM?
explanation: GM is the vertical distance between G and M; if they coincide, the initial metacentric height is zero.

source.label: USCG NMC sample examination topics - Q348

stem: What is a vessel's 'list'?

options.text: A persistent inclination commonly caused by off-center weight or flooding
A periodic roll caused by passing wakes

explanation: List is a sustained tilt away from the upright equilibrium, often due to asymmetric loading or flooding.

source.label: USCG NMC sample examination topics - Q348

stem: Which motion is rotation about the transverse axis?
explanation: Pitch is the vessel's bow-up/bow-down angular motion around a transverse (athwartships) axis.

source.label: USCG NMC sample examination topics - Q348

stem: What does gross tonnage primarily measure?

options.text: Enclosed internal volume according to tonnage rules
Actual weight of the vessel on a scale
Cargo displacement in tons of water

explanation: Gross tonnage is a measure of vessel internal volume under tonnage measurement rules, not vessel weight.

source.label: USCG NMC sample examination topics - Q348

stem: Why must watertight closures be managed carefully during normal operations?

options.text: Open closures can allow progressive flooding across subdivision boundaries
They determine a vessel's call sign
They control the height of navigation lights

explanation: Watertight subdivision works only when the boundary and closures prevent water passing between spaces.

source.label: USCG NMC sample examination topics - Q348

stem: Which of the following is an ordinary combustible Class A fire?
explanation: Class A covers ordinary solid combustibles including wood, cloth, and paper.

source.label: USCG NMC sample examination topics - Q348

stem: A fire involving flammable fuel oil is normally classified as what type?

options.text: Class C only because fuel is onboard

explanation: Class B covers flammable liquids such as gasoline and fuel oil.

source.label: USCG NMC sample examination topics - Q348

stem: What is the defining feature of a Class C fire in common US extinguisher classification?
explanation: Class C addresses energized electrical equipment where a nonconductive extinguishing agent is relevant; de-energizing may change the applicable class.

source.label: USCG NMC sample examination topics - Q348

stem: What normally distinguishes a Class D fire?
explanation: Class D includes fires involving combustible metals such as magnesium or finely divided aluminum/titanium.

source.label: USCG NMC sample examination topics - Q348

stem: What is the fourth element added to the fire triangle to form the fire tetrahedron?
explanation: The fire tetrahedron includes fuel, heat, oxygen, and the sustaining chemical chain reaction.

source.label: USCG NMC sample examination topics - Q348

stem: How does a water stream most commonly suppress a Class A fire?

options.text: By cooling the fuel below a temperature required to sustain burning
By increasing the fire's surface area
By making the fuel more volatile

explanation: Water's principal suppression mechanism for ordinary solid combustibles is heat removal/cooling.

source.label: USCG NMC sample examination topics - Q348

stem: Why can a CO2 extinguisher permit re-ignition of hot fuel after discharge?

options.text: CO2 always increases the fuel's flash point
CO2 adds oxygen to the fire

explanation: CO2 suppresses combustion chiefly by reducing available oxygen and provides limited cooling; hot fuel can reflash when oxygen returns.

source.label: USCG NMC sample examination topics - Q348

stem: Why is discharge of a large CO2 extinguishing system hazardous to personnel in a confined space?

options.text: CO2 can displace breathable oxygen and cause asphyxiation
CO2 always explodes on contact with metal
CO2 is harmless because it is a normal atmospheric gas

explanation: High CO2 concentrations can produce asphyxiation and physiologic toxicity; affected spaces must be evacuated before discharge.

source.label: USCG NMC sample examination topics - Q348

stem: What is an important effect of dry chemical extinguishing agent on a flame?

options.text: It always cools steel below freezing
It removes all fuel from a tank
It turns liquid fuel into water

explanation: Many dry-chemical powders interrupt the chemical chain reactions that sustain a flame.

source.label: USCG NMC sample examination topics - Q348

stem: How does convection commonly spread fire aboard a ship?

options.text: Through movement of hot gases along ventilation pathways
Only by direct contact through a metal bulkhead
Only by radiation across empty space
Through electrical conduction in a copper wire alone

explanation: Convection transfers heat via moving fluids and gases, including smoke and heated air through ducts.

source.label: USCG NMC sample examination topics - Q348

stem: How does conduction move heat aboard a ship?

options.text: Through materials such as steel bulkheads and decks
Only by wind across open deck

explanation: Conduction transfers thermal energy through a material, often allowing heat to spread through metal structures.

source.label: USCG NMC sample examination topics - Q348

stem: What is the first action a crew member should ordinarily take on discovering a shipboard fire?

options.text: Use seawater on energized electrical equipment

explanation: Alerting the crew permits coordinated response and prevents a small fire from remaining undiscovered while one person fights it.

source.label: USCG NMC sample examination topics - Q348

stem: What is the role of the 'pointer' in a person-overboard recovery?

options.text: Maintain continuous visual observation and point toward the person until relieved
Keep the engine at full power

explanation: The pointer tracks the person in the water and provides a continuously visible direction for the helmsman.

source.label: USCG NMC sample examination topics - Q348

stem: What does the liferaft 'painter' usually do during manual deployment?

options.text: Keep the raft attached to the vessel and actuate inflation when pulled fully out
Serve only as an anchor rode after launch
Hold the raft's sea anchor open

explanation: The painter is the line to the raft's inflation mechanism and initial tether; it is secured to the vessel before the canister is launched.

source.label: USCG NMC sample examination topics - Q348

stem: What is the purpose of a hydrostatic release arrangement for a stowed liferaft?

options.text: Permit the raft to release and float free as the vessel sinks when properly installed
Keep the raft permanently attached under all conditions
Prevent the container from ever reaching the surface

explanation: A hydrostatic release unit releases the raft when submerged; the associated painter and weak-link arrangement allows float-free inflation and separation.

source.label: USCG NMC sample examination topics - Q348

stem: What kind of signal does a 406 MHz EPIRB send for rescue alerting?

options.text: A digitally encoded distress signal through the satellite alerting system
A continuous VHF channel 16 voice call
A GPS route automatically uploaded to AIS

explanation: A 406 MHz EPIRB transmits coded distress data detectable by the Cospas-Sarsat satellite system; GPS position can be included when equipped.

source.label: USCG NMC sample examination topics - Q348

stem: Why are periodic EPIRB tests normally performed using the manufacturer's designated test function?

options.text: To avoid transmitting a false distress alert
To ensure a MAYDAY is sent during every test
To recharge the battery by radio waves

explanation: The self-test mode checks selected functions without transmitting an operational distress alert in the normal way.

source.label: USCG NMC sample examination topics - Q348

stem: Why does a personal flotation device light improve survival prospects during a nighttime rescue?

options.text: It helps searchers detect and locate the wearer
It adds buoyancy to the PFD

explanation: A water-activated or manually activated PFD light makes a person in dark water more conspicuous.

source.label: USCG NMC sample examination topics - Q348
